name: On/Off Module

steps.text: Turn on the lamp or appliance.
Unplug the lamp or appliance and plug it into the module's receptacle.
Plug the module into an unswitched wall outlet.
steps.expect: Load turns on and the LED turns green

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds, until the module beeps.
steps.expect: LED blinks green; the module stays in linking mode for four minutes

notes: To link, press and hold the controller's SET button until it beeps, adjust the responder to the desired state, then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps; the controller double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.
As a responder, the module answers by pressing and holding its SET button until it double-beeps while the controller is in linking mode.
If either device's LED keeps blinking, linking failed; tap that device's SET button until the LED stops blinking and try again.
The 3-second hold time comes from the Global Line Developer Notes; software can send the Enter Linking Mode command for the same result.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds, until the module beeps.
steps.expect: LED blinks green; the module stays in linking mode for four minutes

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.
steps.expect: The device acknowledges the Ping

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
steps.expect: LED blinks green

steps.text: Tap the SET button.
steps.expect: LED double-blinks green

steps.text: For each responder, adjust it to the desired scene state.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button.
steps.expect: Module beeps and the LED stops blinking

steps.text: Test by tapping the paddle on and off.
steps.expect: All the responders turn on and off

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
steps.expect: LED blinks green

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps a second time.
steps.expect: LED blinks red; the module is in unlinking mode

notes: To remove a link, put the controller in unlinking mode first, then press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.

To unlink several responders in one session, tap the SET button after entering unlinking mode (LED double-blinks red), press and hold each responder's SET button until it double-beeps, then tap the SET button to finish.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps.
steps.expect: LED blinks green

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps a second time.
steps.expect: LED blinks red

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the module beeps a third time.
steps.expect: LED blinks green

steps.text: Slowly tap the SET button three times.
steps.expect: LED double-blinks green

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button and do not let go.
steps.expect: Module emits a long beep

steps.text: After the beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the module double-beeps

steps.text: For each responder the module controls, put the module in unlinking mode.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
steps.expect: Responder double-beeps

steps.text: For each controller that controls the module, put the controller in unlinking mode.
Press and hold the module's SET button until it double-beeps.
steps.expect: Double beep

notes: The On/Off Module 2633 Owner's Manual says to remove all of the module's responder links before uninstalling it; otherwise controllers keep retrying commands and create network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as the On/Off Module 2633 Owner's Manual gives it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: The 2633-452, sold in Chile on 915 MHz, reports 0x02/0x3A.
